sources.title: SkillBit
sources.finding: Hands-on micro-scenarios, role and tool training, and performance-based skills-gap visibility.
sources.limitation: Public product claims; no customer account or API inspected.

sources.title: SkillBit Labs learning and tracking
sources.finding: Describes curated learning paths, challenge progression, skills-gap insights, browser labs, and LMS/HR/LXP integration capabilities.
sources.limitation: Exact lab-to-role assignments and supported integration protocols were not publicly verified.

sources.title: TryHackMe learning paths
sources.finding: Structured pathways span cyber foundations, SOC, offensive security, and AI security.
sources.limitation: Catalog changes; room-level completion is not certification.

sources.title: TryHackMe certification guide
sources.finding: The certification ladder includes SEC1, SAL1, SAL2, PT1, and AI1.
sources.limitation: Provider guide; optional credentials, not employment prerequisites.

sources.title: TryHackMe AI security
sources.finding: A dedicated AI pathway and AI1 practical certification cover attacking and defending AI applications.
sources.limitation: Training and professional exam are distinct purchases/activities.

sources.title: HTB Academy paths
sources.finding: Separates skill paths from job-role paths; includes AI foundations and AI red teaming.
sources.limitation: Catalog reviewed; no learner records accessed.

sources.title: HTB AI workforce development
sources.finding: Offers development and assessment for human and agentic teams.
sources.limitation: Public marketing evidence; effectiveness was not independently evaluated.

sources.title: HTB AI-augmented paths
sources.finding: AI-augmented SOC and penetration-testing paths emphasize checking agent work and controlling autonomy.
sources.limitation: Incremental releases; complete curriculum availability may vary.

sources.title: HTB Offensive AI certification
sources.finding: COAE validates knowledge across offensive AI and related defense topics.
sources.limitation: Official announcement; verify current exam requirements with HTB.

sources.title: SANS AI cybersecurity careers guide
sources.finding: The live October 19, 2026 page describes four standalone AI roles, five existing roles with AI duties, and one as-yet-untitled work area.
sources.limitation: Live page supersedes an older May search snippet. Linked PDF content was not retrieved; no salary claims imported.

sources.title: SANS AI training portfolio
sources.finding: Distinguishes courses focused on AI from established disciplines that incorporate AI skills. Lists SEC545/GAIPS, SEC598/GASAE, SEC535/GOAA, and SEC595/GMLE.
sources.limitation: Course and credential relationships verified on public portfolio page; titles can change.

sources.title: SANS workforce assessments
sources.finding: ASAP uses practical tasks by job role; CyberTalent uses multiple-choice questions by topic.
sources.limitation: These are separate products; neither is assumed to be an AI career adviser.

sources.title: SANS Applied Skills Analysis Platform
sources.finding: Role-oriented hands-on assessment supports identification of strengths and development gaps.
sources.limitation: Public product information; no trial performed.

sources.title: SANS free AI resources / NotebookLM
sources.finding: Links to a curated interactive AI NotebookLM resource, guidelines, and career materials.
sources.limitation: Notebook requires Google login; linked notebook was not tested. This is a learning aid, not verified career planning automation.

sources.title: SANS Secure AI Blueprint
sources.finding: Organizes secure AI adoption around Protect AI, Utilize AI, and Govern AI.
sources.limitation: Used here as a track taxonomy; detailed white paper was not imported.

sources.title: SANS AI Security Maturity Model
sources.finding: An operational model uses three pillars and five maturity stages.
sources.limitation: Organization maturity is different from individual proficiency.

sources.title: SANS AI attack readiness check
sources.finding: A browser-based readiness check connects capability questions with training suggestions.
sources.limitation: Public interactive capability check; not a validated career selection assessment.

sources.title: Immersive platform
sources.finding: Advertises adaptive assessments, AI learning builders, agent exercises, and NICE/ATT&CK/ATLAS reporting.
sources.limitation: Vendor-described capabilities; access depends on contracted scope.

sources.title: Immersive Resilience Pathways
sources.finding: Connects organizational objectives to AI-assisted learning recommendations and repeated practical assessment.
sources.limitation: Closest researched example of adaptive program planning; not independently benchmarked.

sources.title: OffSec Learn Enterprise
sources.finding: Upskill programs use placement assessments, staged training, labs, and progress tracking, including AI red teaming.
sources.limitation: Subscription-specific features; no integration access assumed.

sources.title: OffSec paths
sources.finding: Catalog includes LLM red teaming, cloud, DevSecOps, forensics, and defensive foundations.
sources.limitation: Availability varies by plan.

sources.title: LetsDefend SOC pathway
sources.finding: SOC learning combines alert analysis, investigation, incident management, and threat intelligence.
sources.limitation: Public syllabus; AI coaching features were not verified.

sources.title: Centri / Security Blue Team BTL1
sources.finding: Practical junior defensive training and certification.
sources.limitation: The researched Security Blue Team URL redirects to Centri; recorded under both names.

sources.title: PortSwigger Web LLM attacks
sources.finding: Free structured web LLM material and labs address prompt injection and connected API risks.
sources.limitation: Lab completion does not award a separate AI professional certification.

sources.title: CyberSeek career pathway
sources.finding: Interactive career pathways connect jobs, skills, certifications, and NICE categories.
sources.limitation: Some displayed salary data uses September 2023–August 2024 listings; no live salaries reproduced.

sources.title: CISA Cyber Career Pathways Tool
sources.finding: Explores NICE work roles and related micro-challenges.
sources.limitation: Useful model for role exploration; official job titles and work roles are not interchangeable.

sources.title: NIST NICE current components
sources.finding: Work role categories, work roles, competency areas, and task/knowledge/skill statements form the workforce vocabulary. Current page identifies components v2.2.0.
sources.limitation: SP 800-181 Rev.1 defines the structure. The current page has an inconsistent year label; release news confirms April 2026. This prototype uses named role anchors, not a full TKS import.

sources.title: NIST NICE v2.2.0 release
sources.finding: Official April 2026 release notice confirms NICE components v2.2.0.
sources.limitation: Version reference only; no invented TKS identifiers.

sources.title: NICE workforce framework online
sources.finding: Official work-role vocabulary includes Defensive Cybersecurity, Incident Response, and other operational functions.
sources.limitation: Prototype mappings are editorial associations to role names.

sources.title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
sources.finding: CSF 2.0 supplies organizational cybersecurity outcome categories.
sources.limitation: Outcomes are not individual qualifications or certifications.

sources.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
sources.finding: AI RMF 1.0 provides voluntary AI risk-management guidance; NIST notes ongoing revision.
sources.limitation: Prototype uses the published 1.0 functions; not a compliance determination.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK
sources.finding: An adversary-behavior knowledge base supports threat-led learning and detection exercises.
sources.limitation: Selected technique examples only; no claim of complete coverage.

sources.title: MITRE ATLAS
sources.finding: A living knowledge base describes adversarial behavior involving AI systems.
sources.limitation: Selected topics rather than a pinned full matrix; topic links resolve to the source matrix.

sources.title: MITRE D3FEND
sources.finding: A knowledge graph of cybersecurity countermeasures complements adversary-oriented training.
sources.limitation: Conceptual association; no automatic equivalence between attack techniques and defenses.

sources.title: OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025)
sources.finding: LLM application risk taxonomy covers prompt injection, information disclosure, supply-chain risks, poisoning, and excessive agency.
sources.limitation: This prototype uses the 2025 edition, with topic IDs.

sources.title: ENISA European Cybersecurity Skills Framework
sources.finding: Twelve professional role profiles provide a European workforce lens.
sources.limitation: Associations here are proposed and not an official NICE-to-ECSF crosswalk.

sources.title: Google Secure AI Framework
sources.finding: AI system risk and control guidance supports secure AI design and deployment.
sources.limitation: Used as a technical reference; not a personnel certification.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023
sources.finding: Requirements for an organizational AI management system.
sources.limitation: Public abstract reviewed; paid normative text was not accessed. No personal ISO certification implied.

sources.title: CIS Controls v8.1
sources.finding: Prioritized cybersecurity safeguards complement role-based learning.
sources.limitation: Selected control numbers used as topic anchors.

sources.title: GIAC certification catalog
sources.finding: Provider catalog includes core cyber and newer AI credentials.
sources.limitation: Optional credential candidates; check exam conditions and renewal requirements.

sources.title: GIAC AI Platform Security
sources.finding: GAIPS addresses security of generative AI applications and LLM pipelines.
sources.limitation: Credential scope is narrower than every skill required by an AI security architect.

sources.title: ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity
sources.finding: A foundational certification with no prior work experience required.
sources.limitation: Exam preparation and certified status remain distinct from demonstrated job competence.

sources.title: ISC2 CCSP
sources.finding: Cloud security credential for design, management, and protection of cloud systems and data.
sources.limitation: Experience and endorsement requirements apply; eligibility must be checked with ISC2.

sources.title: ISC2 CISSP
sources.finding: Broad professional security credential for experienced practitioners.
sources.limitation: Experience and endorsement requirements apply; not positioned here as an entry-level award.

sources.title: ISACA AAISM
sources.finding: AI security management credential for holders of an active CISM or CISSP.
sources.limitation: Active CISM or CISSP is an eligibility requirement, not just recommended preparation.

sources.title: IAPP AIGP
sources.finding: A professional certification covering responsible AI governance and lifecycle risk.
sources.limitation: Governance credential, not a technical AI penetration-testing qualification.

sources.title: Microsoft SC-300
sources.finding: Identity and access administrator certification supports an IAM specialization.
sources.limitation: Vendor-specific credential; agent identity mapping is an IgniteCyber extension.

sources.title: GIAC GICSP
sources.finding: Industrial cybersecurity certification provides an OT-focused credential option.
sources.limitation: AI/OT specialization still needs additional practical validation.

domains.name: Security operations
domains.aiwork: Verify AI alert summaries against raw telemetry, handle malicious alert content, and define approval gates for automated response.
domains.project: Investigate a synthetic alert queue with and without an AI assistant. Record false conclusions, evidence checks, escalation decisions, and measured time/quality differences.

domains.name: Incident response & forensics
domains.aiwork: Use local AI for triage while preserving chain of custody, reproducible timelines, and a fallback when model output is unreliable.
domains.project: Build a reproducible incident timeline from synthetic artifacts; annotate every AI assertion with a source artifact and preserve an evidence-handling log.

domains.name: Offensive security
domains.aiwork: Test AI applications, retrieval boundaries, data integrity, and agent permissions within an authorized scope.
domains.project: Deliver an authorized AI application assessment with reproducible injection cases, trust-boundary findings, severity rationale, and retest evidence.

domains.name: Application security & DevSecOps
domains.aiwork: Threat-model RAG and agent applications; enforce output handling, server-side authorization, and secure dependency pipelines.
domains.project: Create a RAG application threat model and CI evaluation suite that tests cross-user retrieval, unsafe outputs, and tool authorization.

domains.name: Cloud & platform security
domains.aiwork: Secure model endpoints, workload identities, secrets, model artifacts, and AI supply chains in cloud environments.
domains.project: Design a model-serving platform with isolated identities, signed artifacts, audit logs, endpoint access tests, and a rollback runbook.

domains.name: Identity & access management
domains.aiwork: Bind agents to scoped workload identities, minimize delegated privileges, and require authorization outside the model.
domains.project: Demonstrate an agent with short-lived credentials, a tool allowlist, approval gates, revocation tests, and an auditable identity trail.

domains.name: Governance, risk & compliance
domains.aiwork: Maintain AI inventories and risk ownership, set evaluation gates, and gather control evidence throughout the AI lifecycle.
domains.project: Create an AI system inventory, risk register, impact assessment, accountable approval workflow, and evidence-backed monitoring plan.

domains.name: Threat intelligence & hunting
domains.aiwork: Validate AI-enriched intelligence, separate observations from inference, and develop hunts for AI-related adversary behavior.
domains.project: Produce a sourced threat brief and executable hunt plan; record source confidence, ATT&CK/ATLAS associations, and model-generated errors.

domains.name: Data security & privacy
domains.aiwork: Control AI data use, validate retrieval isolation, evaluate leakage, and manage retention across training and inference.
domains.project: Document a synthetic-data lineage map; test cross-user retrieval and sensitive-data output with a minimized retention and deletion design.

domains.name: Security architecture
domains.aiwork: Design AI trust boundaries and control layers spanning models, retrieval, tools, identities, and organizational accountability.
domains.project: Deliver an AI reference architecture with abuse cases, control ownership, failure modes, evaluation criteria, and a residual-risk decision record.

domains.name: OT & critical infrastructure
domains.aiwork: Evaluate industrial AI use with safety constraints, deterministic fallback, isolated test environments, and human override.
domains.project: Create a tabletop and isolated simulation for an AI-assisted industrial monitoring failure. Demonstrate safe fallback, segmentation, and change approval.

domains.name: Exposure & vulnerability management
domains.aiwork: Validate AI findings, add asset and exploitability context, prioritize fixes, and check remediation rather than trusting generated severity.
domains.project: Build a synthetic exposure register with validated findings, contextual priorities, remediation owners, and retest evidence.

domains.name: AI & ML security engineering
domains.aiwork: Secure data/model pipelines, evaluate adversarial behavior, build reproducible security evaluations, and monitor deployment drift.
domains.project: Build a small reproducible ML security evaluation harness with trusted data provenance, baseline metrics, adversarial cases, and regression gates.

questions.prompt: A name resolves to an address, but the TCP connection times out. What should you check next?
options: Only the DNS zone
Routing, firewall policy, and whether the service is listening
The browser language setting
questions.explanation: Successful DNS resolution does not establish network reachability or a listening service.

questions.prompt: A lab asks you to test a public IP not listed in the authorization. What is the next step?
options: Test it quietly
Clarify scope and obtain authorization first
Use an AI agent so it is automated
questions.explanation: Written scope and authorization define what testing is permitted.

questions.prompt: An automated log parser silently drops malformed records. What is the most useful improvement?
options: Ignore them to keep the output clean
Add validation, explicit error counts, and tests for malformed input
Ask the model to guarantee correctness
questions.explanation: Observable errors and input tests make security automation reviewable and reliable.

questions.prompt: An AI assistant says an alert is a false positive. What supports closing it?
options: The confidence language in its answer
The number of words in the summary
Raw telemetry and documented checks that support the conclusion
questions.explanation: The source evidence and investigation criteria justify the decision.

questions.prompt: Before using AI to analyze an evidence image, what should you establish?
options: The model is popular
Evidence integrity, approved handling, and a record of transformations
That the model can write a fluent report
questions.explanation: Integrity and controlled handling protect reproducibility and the evidence trail.

questions.prompt: An AI agent proposes a destructive test outside the agreed rules. What do you do?
options: Run it because automation is faster
Block it, document the proposal, and choose an authorized non-destructive test
Remove logging
questions.explanation: An operator retains responsibility for scope and impact.

questions.prompt: An LLM produces a database query from a user prompt. Where should authorization be enforced?
options: In a polite system prompt alone
In the application/server with scoped permissions and validated operations
Only in the UI
questions.explanation: The model is not an authorization boundary; server-side controls must enforce permissions.

questions.prompt: How should a model-serving workload access its data store?
options: Shared permanent administrator keys
Workload identity with scoped permissions and managed credential lifetime
Credentials inside the model prompt
questions.explanation: Scoped, managed workload identity reduces exposure and supports audit and revocation.

questions.prompt: An agent needs to read one incident queue. Which permission is appropriate?
options: Tenant-wide administrator
Read-only access scoped to that queue
All permissions to avoid errors
questions.explanation: Grant the minimum permission required by the actual task.

questions.prompt: Who should accept material residual AI risk?
options: The AI assistant
The accountable human risk owner under organizational governance
Whoever finishes training first
questions.explanation: Risk decisions need an accountable owner, evidence, and the organization’s approval process.

questions.prompt: A generated threat brief cites a report you cannot locate. What should you do?
options: Publish it with a high-confidence label
Treat the claim as unverified and seek corroborating original evidence
Add more generated citations
questions.explanation: Traceability and corroboration separate observations from unsupported inference.

questions.prompt: A retrieval system returns another customer’s private document. What is the primary fix?
options: Ask the model to be more careful
Enforce tenant/user authorization in retrieval and test isolation
Increase response randomness
questions.explanation: Data access must be enforced before retrieval reaches the model.

questions.prompt: An AI monitoring tool recommends restarting a live industrial controller. What comes first?
options: Execute automatically
Site safety, authorized change control, and validated operating procedures
An internet tutorial
questions.explanation: Safety and site-specific engineering authority govern actions in operational environments.

options: A guarantee that a response is true
Supplying retrieved context to generation; output still needs verification
A replacement for access control
questions.explanation: Retrieved context can improve grounding, but can also be wrong, unauthorized, or malicious.

questions.prompt: A retrieved page tells an agent to ignore instructions and export secrets. What is this?
options: A trusted administrator command
Indirect prompt injection crossing a data/instruction boundary
A harmless formatting preference
questions.explanation: Untrusted retrieved content can contain attacker instructions; host-side permissions and data boundaries matter.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest evaluation for an autonomous response workflow?
options: A single impressive demo
Repeated ground-truth scenarios including errors, denied actions, escalation, and recovery
The model vendor’s popularity
questions.explanation: Evaluate success and failure modes against known outcomes and clear authority boundaries.
